Detection-Feedback Sensitivity Analysis for Population Size

Source: R/feedback_sensitivity.R
feedback_sensitivity.Rd

Relaxes the "no feedback" assumption of the main model, under which detection does not depend on the size of the unauthorized population, and reports the population size consistent with each degree of feedback. The analysis is a deterministic transform of the fitted cell-level estimates: nothing is refitted.

Usage

feedback_sensitivity(
  fit,
  anchor,
  delta_grid = seq(-0.3, 0.3, by = 0.01),
  K = NULL,
  anchor_by = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  total = FALSE,
  boot = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  sublinear = TRUE,
  p_max = 1,
  keep_cells = FALSE,
  delta_prior = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'uncounted_feedback'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'uncounted_feedback'
plot(x, group = NULL, plausible = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fit

An "uncounted" object.

anchor

How to choose \(K_i\), the size at which the main model's detection function is assumed correct. There is no default, because the anchor can reverse the direction of the result (see Details). "geomean" uses the geometric mean of \(\xi_{0i}\) over all cells (or within anchor_by), so "large" means large in absolute terms. "share" uses \(K_i = \bar{s} N_i\) with \(\bar{s}\) the geometric mean of \(\xi_{0i} / N_i\), so "large" means large relative to the reference population. "value" uses K.

delta_grid

Numeric vector of \(\delta\) values. Must contain 0, and every value must exceed \(-1\).

K

Anchor for anchor = "value": a positive scalar, or a positive vector with one value per observation.

anchor_by

Optional one-sided formula: compute the "geomean" or "share" anchor within groups. With ~ country_code the levels of countries barely move, so the analysis concerns changes within countries.

by

Optional one-sided formula for the reported groups, with the same meaning as in popsize.

total

Logical; add a "Total" row when there are several groups? With by = ~ year this adds up the years and is not a population size, because the same people can be present in several years (see popsize). Use it only for non-overlapping groups.

boot

Optional bootstrap_popsize result for the same fit. Its replicate coefficients are transformed; the bootstrap is not re-run. The anchor stays at its point-estimate value in every replicate, because it is part of the assumption rather than an estimate.

level

Level of the percentile bootstrap intervals.

sublinear

Logical; apply constraint A1 (see Details)?

p_max

Upper limit for the implied detection in constraint A2.

keep_cells

Logical; return cell-level matrices in $cells?

delta_prior

Optional Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis (Greenland, 2005): a distribution for \(\delta\) instead of a range. Either list(mean = , sd = ) for a normal distribution truncated to the admissible range, a function of R returning R draws, or TRUE for a uniform distribution on the admissible range. One draw is used per bootstrap replicate, so boot is required. The data do not update this distribution, because \(\delta\) is not identified: the result depends completely on the distribution chosen, so report it and try others.

x

Object to print or plot.

...

Additional arguments passed to plot().

group

For plot(): labels of the groups to draw. Defaults to "Total" when available, otherwise the first six groups.

plausible

For plot(): optional length-2 range of \(\delta\) to mark as plausible.

Value

An object of class "uncounted_feedback", a list with:

profile

Data frame with columns delta, group, estimate, boot_median, lower, upper and admissible.

admissible_range

c(delta_L, delta_U), or NAs when \(\delta = 0\) is inadmissible.

anchor

List with the type, the anchor K per cell, and by.

diagnostics

Data frame per \(\delta\): A1, A2, A3, binding, max_p, max_p_row, and d_total, the derivative of the total with respect to \(\delta\).

a2_excluded

Data frame of the cells left out of A2.

cells

With keep_cells = TRUE: matrices xi, detection and alpha (cells by \(\delta\)). Implied alpha is \(\hat\alpha_i / (1 + \delta)\) for constant anchors, \(1 - (1 - \hat\alpha_i) / (1 + \delta)\) for "share", and NA for "value".

monte_carlo

With delta_prior: data frame with group, median, lower and upper. The \(\delta\) draws are in attr(, "delta") and the totals in attr(, "draws") (groups by replicates), from which changes between years can be computed.

Details

Model. The main model assumes \(E(p_i \mid M_i, N_i, n_i) = \rho_i\). Here \(\delta\) is the elasticity of detection with respect to the unauthorized population \(M_i\):

$$E(p_i \mid M_i, N_i, n_i) = \rho_i (M_i / K_i)^\delta, \qquad \delta > -1,$$

which implies \(\mu_i \approx \rho_i \xi_i (\xi_i / K_i)^\delta\). The approximation treats \(M_i\) as equal to its mean. Holding the fitted \(\hat\mu_i\) and \(\hat\rho_i\) fixed, the population size consistent with \(\delta\) is

$$\xi_i(\delta) = K_i (\xi_{0i} / K_i)^{1 / (1 + \delta)}, \qquad \xi_{0i} = N_i^{\hat\alpha_i}.$$

Fit preservation. Fitted values, likelihood and residuals are the same for every \(\delta\): only the split of \(\hat\mu_i\) into size and detection changes. So \(\delta\) is not identified and the data cannot choose among its values (compare Link, 2003; Barker et al., 2018). Refitting with an offset would not help. The offset model is \(\log\mu_i = (1+\delta)\alpha_i \log N_i + \beta_i \log r_i - \delta \log K\), and because the model has no intercept, the likelihood varies with \(\delta\) only through the normalization \(-\delta \log K\): with \(K = 1\) it does not vary at all.

The anchor is an assumption. \(K_i\) is a pivot: for \(\delta > 0\), cells above it shrink and cells below it grow. Totals are dominated by large cells, so the direction depends on which side of the pivot they lie. Under "geomean" large countries are far above \(K\) and the total falls with \(\delta\). Under "share" they usually have a below-typical \(\xi_{0i} / N_i\), so they lie below \(K_i\) and the total can rise. With "geomean" computed over exactly the summed cells, the total is non-increasing in \(\delta\). Report results under more than one anchor.

Admissibility, from point estimates only:

  • A1 (sublinear = TRUE, constant anchors only): \(\delta > \max_i \hat\alpha_i - 1\), so that size stays sublinear in \(N\). It does not apply to "share" or to a K that varies across cells. With anchor_by, the anchor is constant within groups and A1 is applied.

  • A2: implied detection \(\hat\mu_i / \xi_i(\delta) \le\) p_max. Cells that already exceed p_max at \(\delta = 0\) (possible because the power link does not bound \(\rho_i\)) would make every \(\delta\) inadmissible, so they are left out of A2 with a warning and listed in $a2_excluded.

  • A3: for every group, \(\sum_{i \in g} \xi_i(\delta) \ge \sum_{i \in g} m_i\).

$admissible_range is the largest run of consecutive admissible grid points containing 0, so its ends are limited by delta_grid. The range can hinge on very small cells; $diagnostics shows which constraint binds and where.

Point estimates. estimate uses the plug-in \(\xi_{0i}\), because the analytical bias correction in popsize was derived for \(\delta = 0\). With a bootstrap, boot_median is the recommended point estimate, as in bootstrap_popsize.

References

Barker, R. J., Schofield, M. R., Link, W. A., and Sauer, J. R. (2018). On the reliability of N-mixture models for count data. Biometrics, 74(1), 369–377. doi:10.1111/biom.12734

Greenland, S. (2005). Multiple-bias modelling for analysis of observational data. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series A, 168(2), 267–306. doi:10.1111/j.1467-985X.2004.00349.x

Link, W. A. (2003). Nonidentifiability of population size from capture-recapture data with heterogeneous detection probabilities. Biometrics, 59(4), 1123–1130. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2003.00129.x

See also

feedback_identified_set, feedback_tipping, feedback_calibrate, dependence_bounds, profile_dependence (where delta is a different quantity, a constant shift of the mean)

Examples

set.seed(123)
d <- data.frame(N = round(exp(rnorm(40, mean = 7, sd = 1))))
d$n <- rpois(40, lambda = pmax(1, 0.03 * d$N))
d$m <- rpois(40, lambda = d$N^0.6 * (0.01 + d$n / d$N)^0.6)
fit <- estimate_hidden_pop(d, ~m, ~n, ~N, method = "poisson", gamma = 0.01)

feedback_sensitivity(fit, anchor = "geomean")
#> Detection-feedback sensitivity analysis
#> Anchor: geomean (K = 40.17)
#> The anchor is an assumption and can change the direction of the result.
#> Admissible range: [-0.3, 0.3]
#> 
#> Plug-in estimates:
#>       d=-0.2 d=-0.1 d=0.0 d=0.1 d=0.2
#> (all) 1,894  1,831  1,787 1,754 1,730
feedback_sensitivity(fit, anchor = "share")
#> Detection-feedback sensitivity analysis
#> Anchor: share (K from 5.358 to 229.3)
#> The anchor is an assumption and can change the direction of the result.
#> Admissible range: [-0.3, 0.3]
#> 
#> Plug-in estimates:
#>       d=-0.2 d=-0.1 d=0.0 d=0.1 d=0.2
#> (all) 1,713  1,751  1,787 1,819 1,848
